title: Windows CC build fails with linker out-of-memory (LNK1102) under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation build runs many parallel MSVC link.exe invocations (ninja/cmake parallel build) on a memory-constrained GitHub-hosted Windows runner. Several large test/sample binaries (ov_gpu_unit_tests, ov_api_conformance_tests, ov_transformations_tests, etc.) are linked concurrently; MSVC's link.exe is memory-hungry for large .lib/.obj graphs, and once available RAM is exhausted the linker aborts with LNK1102 ('out of memory') rather than a graceful OOM-kill. This is not caused by the triggering commit's content (a small, type-only OpenCL kernel pointer-cast fix with no functional/link-graph impact) but by resource contention from the existing build parallelism settings on this CI configuration. The same signature (compiler C1060 / linker LNK1102 under high parallelism) has recurred multiple times historically (see pattern 80cfa127185fbf3e), confirming this is a known, persistent CI resource/parallelism issue rather than a one-off.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires reproducing memory pressure on a GitHub-hosted Windows runner identical to the CI environment (limited RAM, many parallel ninja/cmake link jobs). Locally, this can sometimes be approximated by building the same CMake configuration with a high -j parallelism value (e.g., ninja -j<N> matching the runner's job count) on a machine with similarly constrained RAM.
recommended_actions: Reduce the linker/build parallelism for the Windows Conditional Compilation job (e.g., lower CMake/Ninja job pool size via -j or CMAKE_JOB_POOLS for link-heavy targets) to reduce peak concurrent memory usage.

Consider splitting large test targets (ov_gpu_unit_tests, ov_api_conformance_tests, ov_transformations_tests) across build stages or disabling unused test target builds in the Conditional Compilation job if they are not needed for CC coverage.
Evaluate moving this job to a larger-memory Windows runner SKU if available.
Re-run the failed workflow (no code change needed) since this is an infrastructure/resource issue unrelated to the triggering commit.
prevention_strategies: Monitor peak memory usage of the Windows CC build job and set an explicit ninja/cmake link job pool (e.g., JOB_POOLS link=2) to cap concurrent linker processes. Track recurrence via the CI Doctor pattern database and escalate to infra owners once the count crosses a threshold (already recurring, see historical pattern).
historical_context: This exact signature (Windows Release build compiler C1060 / linker LNK1102 out-of-memory under high parallelism) was first recorded on 2026-11-03 (run 41586716106) and has now recurred, confirming a persistent, recurring Windows CI infrastructure/resource-contention issue rather than an isolated incident.
